title: trace
content_html:
trace

Trace of what? In will we leave residues, the question is whether what remains will have a pattern someone can read. A trace can be a minute quantity, a mark left by contact, a line made by following another line or a route reconstructed from surviving signs. A work from residues and a photograph from a doll story each give us something different to follow. Where does the trail go cold, and what does the person doing the tracing leave behind in turn? will we leave residues · Residues 1.1 · Untraceability of Memory

Reading note. Buddhism. In the Khemaka Sutta, washed cloth still carries a scent from the washing. Khemaka uses that residue to speak about a sense of “I am” that lingers after he has ceased to identify himself with any of the five aggregates. The poem will we leave residues raises a question about what such a remainder can do. Can it keep shaping what follows even when no one recognises it? Khemaka Sutta, SN 22.89
